english.title: Record information useful to persons engaged in terrorism
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[collected]_
(B)_[made a record of]_

information of a kind likely to be useful to a person committing or preparing an act of terrorism
english.legislation: Contrary to section 58(1)(a) and (4) of the Terrorism Act 2000.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
collect/make record of
information likely to be useful
to a person committing/preparing
an act of terrorism

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required.
(ii) As per section 58(3), it is a defence for a person charged with an offence under this section to prove that he had a reasonable excuse for his action or possession.
(iii) See section 1 for an interpretation of 'terrorism'.
(iv) The penalty on indictment was increased to include a maximum of 15 years imprisonment from 12 April 2019; for offences from that date, please see document H19992.

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
